items.title: 'I am not angry, I am hot,' says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has again stressed that the government's correct term is the Malaysia Unity Government, saying Umno's support was fundamental to its formation. Zahid then brandished the agreement on cooperation to form the coalition government in front the over 3,000 delegates, saying it specifically referred to the "Malaysia Unity Government." "What I said in my policy speech, I want to show the cooperation agreement to form the coalition government known as the Malaysia Unity Government.

items.title: Zahid: Umno will not blindly follow those seeking to dictate its direction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has taken another swipe at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying the party will not blindly follow those seeking to dictate its political direction. "The Umno General Assembly is not only followed by party members. Zahid said Umno had its own political independence and leadership to determine the party's direction.

items.title: Home Ministry to announce effective date for citizenship amendments once ready
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 12 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will announce the effective date of amendments to citizenship provisions for children born overseas to Malaysian women once all preparations for their implementation have been completed. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the preparations included the relevant documentation, citizenship regulations and an online application system, which would also involve Malaysian representative offices worldwide. He said that out of approximately 50,000 outstanding citizenship applications that previously needed to be processed, about 7,000 involved children born overseas to Malaysian mothers.

items.title: Zahid: Dewan Merdeka may witness Umno-BN return to power in 2026/2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi believes Dewan Merdeka could witness the return of Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) to power as early as 2026 or 2027. "Whether in early, middle or late 2026 or 2027, this hall will witness Umno and BN back in power," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly. He said the Dewan Merdeka had also witnessed past leadership disputes, the banning of Umno and major internal crises that tested the party's survival.

items.title: Zahid says door for Umno-PAS cooperation ‘wide open’, eyes million-strong unity rally ahead of GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The presence of PAS leaders at this year’s Umno general assembly signals the potential for Malaysia’s two largest Malay-based parties to cooperate again, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan led a delegation of his party leaders to the Umno assembly opening yesterday. Zahid also instructed Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh to work with his counterparts in PAS and gather over a million Malay-Muslims for a mammoth rally he dubbed “Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah”.

items.title: 'Tekad 16' to guide Umno's preparations for GE16, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno has agreed to adopt "Tekad 16" as an official party programme to prepare for the 16th General Election (GE16). Its president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the initiative would focus on five priorities: strengthening the party, closing ranks, strengthening its election machinery, refining its strategy and reaching out to the people. Tekad 16.

items.title: Deal directly with DBKL for trading lots to avoid scams, says Hannah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Traders seeking micro-financing and trading lots are advised to deal directly with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) rather than third-party agents to avoid falling victim to scams. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said those interested, particularly low-income groups, should approach DBKL officers directly. "I advise anyone interested to apply, especially those in Kuala Lumpur who are listed under eKasih, to contact DBKL directly.

items.title: BN can win Pahang with PH or PN, says Wan Rosdy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan for the 16th General Election (GE16) could result in BN losing 15 per cent of Malay voter support in Pahang, said Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. The Umno vice-president, however, said BN could still win the state if it worked with PH. Wan Rosdy said Pahang Umno had held three retreats involving himself, fellow Umno leaders and division chiefs to discuss the matter.

items.title: Umno’s exit from unity govt would demand fresh mandate, not backroom deal, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today that the party's removal from the unity government would require a fresh mandate to determine the country's next administration. He said there would be only two options if Umno were asked to leave the government: hold a general election to obtain a fresh mandate, or formally remove the party and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat. “Don't ask us to leave the government.

items.title: Zahid reveals past attempts to pit him against Tok Mat
items.summary: "Tok Mat, elok-eloklah jadi timbalan (Tok Mat, be careful in your role as deputy). Sustenance never comes to the wrong address, Tok Mat. Tok Mat, that was a story from the past.

items.title: Heli crash: Captain Zainol, Dr Ainul Baraah's remains expected to be buried tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The remains of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, are expected to be brought back to Negeri Sembilan tomorrow for burial at the Senawang Muslim Cemetery (Forest Heights) after Asar prayers. "The remains are expected to arrive at Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque at 4.30 pm before being taken to the Senawang Muslim Cemetery (Forest Heights), where the burial is expected to take place at 5.30pm," he told Bernama today. Meanwhile, the remains of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, are expected to arrive in Kelantan tomorrow morning.

items.title: ‘One for you, one for me’: Tok Mat calls for PAS to put its unity talk to the test after Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno should press for snap elections in one of the four states ruled by Perikatan Nasional to test the sincerity of PAS, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. Mohamad, popularly known as Tok Mat, said the era of one-party rule was over, but Umno should not let other parties take advantage of its generosity in political pacts. “Ask them to hold elections in one of the SG4 states,” the Umno deputy president said, using the initials for the four state governments controlled by PAS — Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.

items.title: Temerloh crash claims fifth victim after teenager dies
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The death toll from the 11-vehicle crash at Km 110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) on Sept 1 has risen to five after another victim died yesterday. His father, Seow Beng Wain, was among the four victims who died at the scene. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron confirmed the teenager's death when contacted today.

items.title: Umno to hold 'Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah' with Pas to test political cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has given the party's Youth wing a mandate to organise a "Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah" aimed at bringing together one million Muslims as part of efforts to strengthen cooperation with Pas. Zahid said the presence of Pas leaders at the Umno General Assembly yesterday was a positive signal of growing room for understanding between the two parties. "We will engage in political cooperation with them," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin calls for capital, climate action, innovation for resilient future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah has called for capital, climate action and innovation to be brought together in a concerted effort to build a more resilient and sustainable future. In his royal address titled Building Resilience: The Intersection Between Capital, Climate and Innovation at the 17th SC-OCIS Roundtable, Sultan Nazrin said these three priorities were often discussed separately, despite being closely interconnected and essential to addressing the challenges facing future generations. He said the world was increasingly seeing the consequences of treating capital and climate as unrelated concerns.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: King has sole power to grant pardons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The power to grant pardons rests solely with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong as provided for under the Federal Constitution, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said. She said any further clarification on the matter had already been detailed in a media statement released by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department. When asked when the Pardons Board would convene its next meeting, Yeoh said members of the board would be notified accordingly.

items.title: Zahid orders free flights for B40 students from Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir has been directed to ask universities to provide free flight tickets for B40 students from Sabah and Sarawak studying in Peninsular Malaysia. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had also instructed the menteris besar of Johor, Negri Sembilan, Pahang and Perak, as well as the Melaka Chief Minister, to provide free flight tickets for B40 students from their respective states studying in Sabah and Sarawak. Zahid, who is also Umno president, said this in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Male elephant roaming near Terengganu village caught, now on a banana diet
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Sept 12 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a wild male elephant that was roaming in Kampung Kolam, Ajil, near here on Thursday. He said the elephant would be fed banana trunks twice a day by the department staff before being relocated to a suitable location. On Sept 10, the Hulu Terengganu Wildlife Department office received a report regarding a wild elephant roaming in Kampung Kolam.

items.title: Zahid: Ceplos, do not challenge Umno to leave unity government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded those calling for the party to leave the unity government that Umno played an important role in its formation. "Ceplos... do not challenge Umno to leave the unity government," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly. "The unity government was formed because of Umno, you know.

items.title: Umno must turn Malaysia Blue Agenda into grassroots action, says Wan Rosdy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must translate its Malaysia Blue Agenda into sustained grassroots efforts to strengthen public confidence ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. He said the agenda, introduced by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, would not move forward on its own and required the involvement of all party members. Wan Rosdy said the party also needed to strengthen public trust through tangible service and give people reasons to continue having confidence in Umno.

items.title: Nurses wanted: Public Service Commission says 400 posts still open despite hiring push
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 12 — The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process. Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang. Ahmad Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.

items.title: Fatal Desa Green accident not a hit-and-run, say police
items.summary: Donny added that the driver, a 60-year-old retiree, was uninjured. "The driver was subsequently traced and lodged a police report at 10.38pm the same day," Donny said. Donny added that the driver, a 60-year-old retiree, was uninjured.

items.title: Zahid warns against challenging Umno to leave unity government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has warned against challenging the party to leave the unity government. The deputy prime minister said any move to remove Umno should instead be followed by a fresh mandate from voters or a no-confidence vote in the Dewan Rakyat. First, obtain a fresh mandate by holding a general election.

items.title: From speech to GE16 manifesto: BN locks in Blue Malaysia Agenda
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Blue Malaysia Agenda outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will be reflected in Barisan Nasional’s (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), says BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the agenda formed part of the coalition’s efforts to formulate an approach that ensured Malaysia remained peaceful and stable, while navigating current and future challenges. Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said Umno and BN would outline the Blue Malaysia Agenda to shape the nation’s trajectory heading towards the centenary of its independence, should the coalition return to lead Putrajaya.

items.title: [UPDATED] Tok Mat proposes Terengganu polls to test political partners' sincerity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has proposed that one of the "SG4" states, specifically Terengganu, hold an election to test prospective political partners' sincerity in pursuing cooperation. He said this would show whether cooperation in the name of Malay-Muslim unity reflected a genuine willingness to share power or merely benefited one side. Let us ask one of the SG4 states to hold an election.

items.title: RM60,000 versus RM500,000: Penang chief minister says still weighing DAP’s call for equal funding law
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — The Penang government is unlikely to table a proposed law guaranteeing equal constituency development funds (CDF) at the coming state legislative assembly sitting, due to time constraints. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said he had instructed the state legal adviser to prepare a draft enactment. He said the state government needed time to examine its details, adding that an engagement session with stakeholders would also be required.

items.title: Kon Yeow orders excos to clear unfinished Penang2030 projects before he steps down as chief minister
items.summary: He said the directive was issued several weeks ago, and that he was personally monitoring the outstanding initiatives. Chow said he would seek explanations from state excos overseeing portfolios that had recorded slow progress. “Penang has established 384 urban farms, but agricultural productivity remains below the state’s target,” he said during his presentation.

items.title: [UPDATED] Era of single-party government is over, says Tok Mat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The days of a single party forming the government on its own are over, said Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. "Let us not dream that one party can form the government, that Umno can form the government on its own," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly. Citing Johor, he said strong "Bangsa Johor" sentiment had been reinforced by the state government's performance under Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.

items.title: [UPDATED] Tok Mat: Umno must rebuild its strength as others seek its downfall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has reiterated his call for the party to build its own strength, warning that other parties want to see its downfall. He said Umno could not rely on others to help it regain its strength and must learn from past disappointments. They all want to see us buried," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Khaled warns of cognitive warfare threats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry is stepping up efforts to counter growing cognitive warfare threats, including disinformation, digital propaganda and the use of artificial intelligence to influence how Malaysians think and act. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such threats were no longer confined to conventional warfare but had evolved into hybrid forms that could exploit technology and social divisions. The Umno vice-president said there were already efforts to systematically use artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies to influence public opinion and behaviour.

items.title: Malays should learn from Chinese political unity, says Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malays should learn from the way the Chinese community works together politically despite belonging to different parties, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. Khaled said Chinese political groups might disagree and engage in fierce political debate, but remained united when issues affecting the community's long-term interests arose. Khaled said this approach had enabled different Chinese political groups to maintain a common position on issues they regarded as important to the community.

items.title: As new law on campus politics takes shape, minister sorts students into two camps — ‘Agree’ and ‘Disagree’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Discussions are under way with all relevant parties on the drafting of a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. He said the new law should not only take into account current needs, but also address the challenges the country may face in the future. “I have said repeatedly that UUCA was introduced 54 years ago.

items.title: Umno to decide on proposal to raise Puteri membership age limit after GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will decide on a proposal to raise the age limit for Puteri Umno membership only after the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. Khaled, who chairs the party's Constitution and Rules Committee, said the proposal required careful consideration as any change would affect not only Puteri Umno but also Wanita Umno and the party as a whole. He said the proposal had received strong support from Puteri Umno, but the party needed to assess its wider implications before making a decision.

items.title: Sabah tourism players seek package tour subsidies
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah tourism players have urged the government to introduce targeted package tour subsidies to help offset airfares between Kuala Lumpur and Kota Kinabalu ahead of Visit Sabah Year 2027. They also urged closer coordination with the Sabah Water Department, Kota Kinabalu City Hall and authorities to give hotel operators notice of water supply disruptions, after at least 10 hotels in Kota Kinabalu were recently affected. They called for long-term planning around fuel pricing and consideration of bringing licensed tourism transport operators into the subsidised diesel control system scheme.

items.title: Come set up shop in KL, Anwar says to Ethiopia after decades apart
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended an invitation to Ethiopia to establish an Embassy in Kuala Lumpur during his bilateral meeting with his counterpart, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Malaysia’s reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after 43 years, marked significant progress in bilateral relations. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Malaysia in 2024, while Anwar visited Ethiopia in 2025.

items.title: Anwar, Modi discuss expanding Malaysia-India ties in semiconductor sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi have discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in strategic sectors, particularly the semiconductor industry. Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Malaysia and India possess complementary strengths that could be harnessed through industrial cooperation, supply chain integration, talent development, and bilateral investment. Anwar met Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi after arriving in India with the Malaysian delegation last night.

items.title: Lack of political will prolonging Sabah's migrant problem, says ex-CJ Malanjum
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's long-standing undocumented migrant problem continues because of a lack of political will to implement proposed solutions, says former chief justice Tun Richard Malanjum. He said numerous proposals had been put forward over the years - from recalling wrongfully issued identity cards to introducing a distinct Sabah identity card, a kad warga asing and a pas sementara Sabah - only to be abandoned. The book, authored by Sessions Court judge Dr Melissa Chia, is based on court cases, notes of proceedings from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), archival material from the Sabah Archives and Sabah government, and field interviews.

items.title: Analysts: Umno-Pas cooperation carries political risks and opportunities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Closer political cooperation between Umno and Pas could offer political gains but also risks, analysts said, as Umno prepares to form a committee to explore cooperation with Pas. Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the proposed understanding would allow Umno to keep its options open while assessing whether closer cooperation with Pas was politically viable, including gauging the reactions of its grassroots, Pas and existing political partners. Umno and Pas have traditionally competed for Malay-Muslim voters, making closer cooperation between the two parties politically significant.

items.title: NSE southbound lane near Menora Tunnel reopens after slope deemed safe
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 12 — The left lane of the North-South Expressway (NSE) southbound at KM263.6, which was temporarily closed following a landslide yesterday, has been reopened to all vehicles at 1pm today. “As such, the southbound left lane was reopened to all vehicles at 1pm. Earlier, the left lane at the landslide site at KM263.6 of the North-South Expressway (southbound) was closed, spanning about one kilometre.

items.title: Development must not come at expense of values, says Melaka Umno delegate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must prioritise instilling patriotic and moral values among young Malaysians alongside its pursuit of development, a Melaka delegate said. Alor Gajah Umno division deputy chief Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa said nurturing these values must begin at a young age, with the principles of the Rukun Negara serving as a foundation. "We must start here.

items.title: Police hunt two men who rammed patrol car to escape inspection in Kajang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are searching for two men who rammed a patrol car and a civilian vehicle to escape an inspection along Jalan Semenyih near the Kajang Prima traffic lights yesterday afternoon. Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said a mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) attempted to inspect a green Proton Wira at 3.15pm. "The police MPV sustained damage to the right front door, but no civilians or police personnel were injured," Naazron said.

items.title: Anwar-Modi Brics meeting: Semiconductor ties, bilateral trade take centre stage
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi discussed deepening semiconductor cooperation and translating it into industry partnerships during their bilateral meeting here today. Anwar spoke about integrated supply chains, talent development and two-way investment during the meeting held on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to increasing bilateral trade and investment, enhancing cooperation across various sectors, as well as implementing measures to facilitate and expedite Malaysian exports to India.

items.title: Anwar, Modi task Ramanan with coordinating Malaysia-India business platform
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, have agreed to task Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan with coordinating efforts to establish a platform connecting the Malaysian and Indian business communities. The agreement was reached during their meeting today as part of efforts to strengthen Malaysia-India economic ties, expand business networks and create new investment opportunities between the two countries. "This platform is not merely about connecting the business communities of the two countries.

items.title: ‘My brother’: PM Anwar, Modi meet on Brics sidelines
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — “My brother” had the rare honour of becoming the warm greeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi at their bilateral meeting here today. The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 18th Bric Leaders’ Summit at the Hyderabad House, which is the State Guest House under the Ministry of External Affairs. It is used for bilateral meetings, state banquets and meetings with foreign leaders.

items.title: A spring in Umno’s step: Three things we learnt from its 2026 general assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno’s annual general assembly ended yesterday with a sense of optimism rarely seen at the party’s recent assemblies, as delegates filled the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur with renewed enthusiasm for the party. Umno members gather for the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. Umno members wave party flags during the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026.

items.title: After Bandar Tasik Selatan PPR gets RM350,000 makeover, MP asks residents to ‘take good care’ for sake of kids and grandkids
items.summary: Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said repair works on the lifts at the apartments would also be carried out soon to ensure residents’ comfort. We must work together to develop and maintain them so that our children and grandchildren can also enjoy the benefits,” she said while officiating the Bandar Tun Razak Parliamentary Constituency Kenduri Rakyat Madani 2026 programme here today. Dr Wan Azizah said the initiative demonstrated how collaboration among the community, management bodies and the private sector could deliver better facilities for residents.

items.title: ‘We still have until February 2028’, Pakatan sec-gen says as GE16 chatter grows
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today brushed aside calls for the 16th general election to be held earlier, saying the Madani government’s term only expires in February 2028. Saifuddin Nasution was responding to questions from reporters after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here, national news agency Bernama reported. Anwar is from the same party and coalition as Saifuddin Nasution.

items.title: Were the 30 Malaysians caught in Indonesia lone scammers, or something bigger? Home Ministry to dig deeper
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country’s authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter. Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani Government’s focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.

items.title: Foreign Ministry seeks DNA samples of Nepal flood victims to identify missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is reportedly in talks with Nepal to have DNA samples from flood victims found during search-and-rescue operations sent here for matching against samples taken from relatives of Malaysians who remain missing, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. According to Utusan Malaysia , Mohamad said the initiative was proposed because Nepalese authorities face shortages of facilities and equipment needed to identify victims. Mohamad reportedly said Malaysia was also considering sending DNA experts to Nepal, while the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked Nepalese security authorities to forward samples already collected from recovered victims.

items.title: Mission done, but not over: Smart team on way home as Nepal search continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission in Nepal, is expected to return home today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. “The Smart team leader will provide a report and assess the next steps so that we do not make hasty decisions; if they (Nepal) require assistance from Malaysia, we can consider helping with the search or rescue operations,” he said. The Smart MAS01 team, participating in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission to Nepal, arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on September 5.

items.title: Anwar to Iran: Keep Hormuz open, choose diplomacy over conflict
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed concern over the continued conflict and escalation across West Asia during a bilateral meeting with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian today. “Malaysia urged all parties to return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve disputes and de-escalate the situation,” the prime minister said during a 30-minute meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the summit here. Anwar, who is also finance minister, welcomed Putrajaya and Tehran’s long-standing diplomatic relations and reaffirmed cooperation on various fronts.

items.title: Umno won’t ‘betray anyone’ or seek new PM before next general election, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said the party would not seek to change the prime minister or form a new government before the next general election is called. He said Umno remained committed to political stability and had yet to begin negotiations for the next general election. Speculation over Umno strengthening political ties with PAS intensified after PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and several other senior party leaders attended the Umno General Assembly yesterday.

items.title: Stop hunting for jobs, start creating them, minister tells TVET grads as 97pc find work
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 12 — The Ministry of Youth and Sports (KBS) provides avenues and opportunities for graduates with disabilities, including those with autism, to enter the workforce, including the public service, after completing their studies at the Youth and Sports Skills Training Institutes (ILKBS). Its Minister, Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, said the ministry maintained data on ILKBS graduates and alumni each year to track their career paths, with most securing opportunities in the industry, as well as in the private and public sectors. Mohammed Taufiq said 4,155 graduates received their certificates at this year’s convocation after completing diploma, advanced certificate and skills certificate programmes in various fields offered by ILKBS, including 130 youths with disabilities and autism.

items.title: Empty posts, crumbling clinics: Sarawak wants the power to fix its own healthcare
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — Sarawak is pushing for regulatory powers under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586) to be decentralised to the state Health Department (JKNS), said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian. Dr Sim also called for urgent action to address Sarawak’s shortage of health personnel, with 5,654 vacant posts currently under JKNS. Dr Sim said health was among the more complex MA63 matters, involving 41 laws.

items.title: Early morning blaze guts first floor of Kuching retail chain, no injuries reported
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — A fire broke out at a retail chain near Jalan Tun Ahmad Zaidi Adruce here early on Saturday morning. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (better known locally as Bomba) dispatched firefighters from the Batu Lintang fire station after receiving a call at around 3.42am. “The fire broke out on the first floor involving various goods.

items.title: Lawyer denies govt forfeited funds in Abdul Azeez family’s Tabung Haji accounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A lawyer for former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has reportedly denied claims that the government forfeited RM18 million held in TH accounts belonging to his family members. Instead, Amer reportedly said the charge read out at the Sessions Court on September 8 alleged that Azeez used his position as TH chairman to obtain the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which brought benefits including annual remuneration, a vehicle and a permanent driver. Amer also reportedly said the Royal Commission of Inquiry into TH had made no finding that Azeez had taken or misappropriated TH funds for himself or his family, adding that Azeez has pleaded not guilty to the charge.

items.title: Economy minister says Malaysia to deepen renewable energy, connectivity ties with Indonesia, Thailand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is committed to strengthening regional cooperation in the field of renewable energy and connectivity as an effort to expand economic opportunities at the sub-regional level of Asean, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said that sub-regional approaches such as the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT) can strengthen the economic potential among member countries through the implementation of more structured and effective plans. FDI inflows increased from US$27.52 billion (RM112.1 billion) to US$28.44 billion (RM115.9 billion), while the unemployment rate declined from 3.8 per cent to 3.7 per cent, reflecting the subregion’s economic resilience.

items.title: Sarawak dialysis patient’s rescue shows why the Flying Doctor Service matters
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 12 — When a helicopter crashed just 200 metres from her home in Long Lellang, Renai Iwat was not only confronted with the trauma of losing a vital link to medical care, but also another race against time. Renai was eventually airlifted from Long Lellang to Miri Hospital on Thursday (Sept 10) by a Bomba helicopter, allowing her to resume the treatment on which she depends. Renai Iwat seated aboard the Bomba helicopter en route to Miri Hospital, accompanied by rescue personnel after her successful medical evacuation from Long Lellang.

items.title: No special treatment in Peter Anthony’s release, says Prisons Department
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia’s Prisons Department said the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme (PBSL) was granted after he met the required eligibility period and underwent the same screening and assessment process as other prisoners considered for the programme. However, serving this minimum period does not automatically qualify a prisoner for release under PBSL,” it added. “Regarding the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony, the Prisons Department stresses that consideration for his participation in PBSL was made after he reached the prescribed eligibility period and underwent the screening and assessment process applied to other candidates considered for the programme,” it said.

items.title: DNA results of Long Lellang crash victims finally in, families set to receive remains
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 12 — The DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) test results for the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang in Baram have been obtained, and the remains will be handed over to the next of kin today, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah. Meanwhile, funeral arrangements are under way for three of the five victims, as their families prepare to bid their final farewells. Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry will be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir following a funeral service at the Good Shepherd Church in Lutong at 9 am on Sept 15.
